note: Out-of-sample: each week scored on the weekly-projections file committed last before its first kickoff, against actual PPR for players who played. Methods are compared on the same player-weeks. flat = season line only (no matchup layer); benchmark = an external projection set's error on the same rows (its projections are an input and are not published). calibration.slope = how much of the projected matchup swing showed up (1 = right size); impliedScale = the per-position POS_MATCHUP_SCALE the data asks for. noShowStarters = players projected ≥ 8 as active starters who did not play.

statLines.note: Per-week stat lines scored on the same player-weeks: ours = the feed's split (statRule per week: split = volume flat, yards / TDs carry the swing; proportional = every component × the multiplier, reconstructed from the pool for weeks before the feed carried statsPG), flat = the season per-game stat, benchmark = the external set's stat. swingSlope = slope of (actual − flat) on (projection − flat) for that component: 1 = right size, 0 = the matchup carries no information about it.

picks.note: Recorded pick lines (scripts/price-lines.py --record) graded once the week is final: hit = the recorded lean was right (a push is void), ret = the return per 1 unit at the recorded payout (mult - 1 on a hit, -1 on a miss), roi = return per pick. expectedHitRate = the mean calibrated probability the model gave its leans (rawExpectedHitRate the simulation's raw share), so hitRate against each is the calibration check that re-tunes the shrink. byTag: call = picks we actually made (price-lines.py --tag call), auto = leans the scheduled run recorded. byMove: by how the book moved the line after we recorded it (track-lines.py), toward our lean or away. void: the player was inactive, no bet. flagged = picks that carried a guardrail flag when recorded.

bands.note: Two bands, both conditional on playing. tier: empirical quantiles of actual / projected (players who played) by position and projection tier, each position shrunk toward the pooled tier shape by n / (n + 40); a band is the projection × these ratios. simulation: the player's own outcome distribution from his projected stat line — volume gamma around its projection with the log-dispersion of its projected-volume tier (volumeSigmaTier, volumeSigma the fallback), receptions binomial at his catch rate, yards = the sum over those opportunities of a gamma per-opportunity yardage (yardsShape = the gamma shape; yardsPerOppSigma is the game-level log-dispersion it was fitted from), TDs Poisson at his rate per opportunity (negative binomial where tdDispersion > 1), INTs Poisson — each draw scored; a TD-dependent or low-volume line gets a wider band. Gamma rather than lognormal because the lognormal median sat too low (walk-forward on 2026: 42% of receivers' actual yards below the simulated median vs 49% with gamma). Published band = the average of the two quantile sets (simulation.coverage.blend checks it). The median sits below the projection because weeks are right-skewed. coverage = share of last week's actuals inside the bands fitted on the weeks before it (80% band should read ~0.80, 50% band ~0.50).
